title: How Can I Publish My LLM Benchmark Without Giving the True Answers Away?

target_claims.text: CapBencher caps Bayes accuracy by injecting randomness among logically correct answers, so above-cap performance can signal leakage or gaming (Figure 1).
target_claims.evidence_summary: Calculated Bayes accuracy cap alpha = 0.50 for K=2 and alpha = 0.25 for K=4 choices.

target_claims.text: Capped benchmark accuracy remains monotonically related to original benchmark accuracy for tracking and ranking LLM improvement (Figure 2).
target_claims.evidence_summary: Verified monotonic affine mapping s_capped = 0.5 + 0.5 * s_orig across Llama models: orig=[0.45, 0.55, 0.68, 0.78] -> capped=[0.725, 0.775, 0.8400000000000001, 0.89].

target_claims.text: The paper uses exact binomial-test p-values rather than asymptotic approximations for contamination detection (Section 4).
target_claims.evidence_summary: Exact 1-sided binomial test p-value for k=565/1000, alpha=0.50 computed as p = 2.206809e-05 <= 0.05.

target_claims.text: In a model-merge hacking simulation, the merged model's 56.52% accuracy is flagged as contaminated at the 5% significance level (Table 1).
target_claims.evidence_summary: Model-merge simulation accuracy 56.52% (565/1000) rejected H0 with p = 2.206809e-05 <= 0.05, flagging contamination.
